Daily Brief

The day's most significant developments center on escalating climate emergencies and fragile diplomatic openings. Catastrophic wildfires across southwestern France and Spain have displaced over 325,000 people, with flames now within 15 kilometers of Bordeaux as another heatwave approaches [RFI, France 24, The Hindu]. President Macron has convened a crisis cabinet meeting. Meanwhile, a tentative pause in hostilities between the US and Iran—marking the second consecutive day without strikes—has sent oil prices tumbling more than 7% and opened a narrow window for renewed negotiations [France 24, Le Monde, Financial Times, The Hindu]. In Berlin, a 24-hour manhunt ended when police shot and killed Abdul Ballout, the suspect in Saturday's Pride attack that killed one and injured 29; German authorities have characterized the incident as an Islamist terror attack [BBC, RFI]. India's student protest movement secured a rare political victory as Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following weeks of demonstrations over exam system failures [BBC, France 24, Al Jazeera]. In financial markets, Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT surged 465% in its Shanghai debut, surpassing Intel's market capitalization in Asia's largest IPO of the year [Nikkei Asia, Financial Times].
